segment.description: Little Sequatchie River in Marion County (catalog county), the Sequatchie-valley tributary that joins the Sequatchie River drainage reaching the Tennessee River/Nickajack pool — verified distinct from the Sequatchie River itself (separate stations 03571000/03571610 on the Sequatchie vs 03571485/03571500 on the Little Sequatchie) and from Cumberland-Plateau namesakes. The two agency stations with data both sit on the cataloged Marion County lower river: USGS 03571500 'LITTLE SEQUATCHIE RIVER AT SEQUATCHIE, TN' (35.1298, -85.5861, 116 sq mi drainage) and TDEC TDECWPC-LSEQU000.5MI 'LITTLE SEQUATCHIE RIVER NEAR MOUTH' (35.0946, -85.5736).
segment.boundaries: Full Marion County reach of the river (HUC-8 06020004, Sequatchie), from the headwater area downstream to the mouth at ~35.0946, -85.5736. All temperature evidence is from the lower river near Sequatchie/Whitwell; no data was located for upstream reaches.

coldSource.notes: Catalog describes the stream as 'spring-influenced... modest, steady flows by Highland Rim standards' — that is an editorial catalog note; no agency page located this session documents spring inflow to this river. The measured summer grabs at the two lower-river stations (22.0-28.0 degC in July) bound whatever spring influence exists. No elevation figure published on an agency page.

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence found: no creel data, holdover notes, or multiple independent angler reports were located for the Little Sequatchie River.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found: the river carries no entry on TWRA's trout-regulations lists (wild trout waters / special regulation / delayed harvest — the wave-3 verification explicitly confirmed no Little Sequatchie entry), and no fish-community inventory documenting trout was located.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Two independent agency stations on the lower Marion County river both recorded July maxima hostile to trout — 28.0 degC (USGS 03571500, 1980) and 22.0 degC (TDEC near-mouth station, 2001) — and TWRA's own program treats the water as a seasonal spring-stocked put-and-take (Mar 15, Mar 22, May 10 2026 weeks only).
